# v1.1.0-dev.82 — The display editor stops freezing, and starts remembering

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.81`.

## The Freeze Was One Line, And It Has Been There Since dev.74

Applying or reverting a display change sometimes locked the app up. The
cause turned out to be a function that called itself.

WLM pushes events to its windows through one helper. Its job is to send to
the main window and then to each open dialog, because dialogs became
separate windows back in dev.74. The line meant to send to the main window
called the helper again instead. It recursed until it ran out of stack. The
error it threw landed in an empty catch, which is why nothing ever appeared
in a log.

Two things followed from that. Both were invisible. The main window
received none of those events at all. Every open dialog received one copy
per level of the recursion, which is thousands of them. The display editor
is a dialog. Applying a display change is one of those events. That
combination is what buried it.

Anything the app pushes rather than answers went through that helper:
hotkey updates, the "profile loaded" toast, live profile changes, the
result of a display apply. All of it reaches the main window again now, for
the first time since dev.74.

Two smaller things on the same path went with it. An internal busy flag was
raised just outside the block that clears it. One unlucky error could
therefore leave it stuck on, refusing every later apply for as long as the
app stayed open. And a refused revert looked exactly like a successful one.
The status line said your displays were put back whether or not they were,
while the snapshot needed to try again had already been thrown away. A
revert that cannot run now says so, and stays on screen so you can press it
again.

## Save The Arrangement You Already Have

Pinning your monitor layout into a profile only worked if you dragged
something. If your monitors were already sitting exactly the way you
wanted, there was nothing to drag, no button to press, and Save quietly
wrote no arrangement at all. The state most worth capturing was the one
state you could not capture.

The picker now says which of three things is true, and offers the matching
control:

- **Not saved with this profile**, with **Save this arrangement**. Pin the
  desk exactly as it stands.
- **Changed from your current arrangement**, with **Revert**.
- **Saved with this profile**, with **Remove arrangement**.

Those last two used to be one button sharing one handler, which had a sharp
edge. Pressing **Revert** to undo a stray drag also deleted the arrangement
the profile already carried. Silently, one Save later. Revert puts the
boxes back and nothing else now.

## Earlier Arrangements, With A Preview

The Keep-or-Revert countdown covers the change you just made. It does not
cover the one from yesterday.

WLM now records your monitor arrangement before every change, whatever
caused it: a profile load, a hotkey, the editor's Apply now, even a restore
from this list. **History** in the display editor shows them newest first,
with what caused each one and how long ago it was.

**Preview** draws an entry in the picker at the top of the editor. Nothing
is applied. Nothing on your desk moves. You can click straight down the
list comparing them. **Restore this one** is the separate, deliberate step
that actually writes it, going through the same 15-second Keep-or-Revert
countdown as everything else.

The list is tied to the monitors it describes. A layout recorded at your
desk is therefore never offered to you on a different set of displays. An
entry naming a monitor you no longer have is shown greyed out and says
which one is missing, rather than disappearing and leaving you wondering
where your history went.

## Windows Stay On The Monitor They Were On

Moving a monitor in the editor left your windows behind. Windows all live
in one coordinate space. A display that moves therefore changes which
physical screen a given position lands on. Swap your left and right
monitors and everything that was on the right kept the same coordinates,
which put it on the left, or off the desktop entirely. Windows itself only rescues the ones
that end up completely off-screen.

Windows now follow the monitor they were on, keeping the same spot on it.
This runs once, straight after the arrangement lands, and is finished when
it returns. Minimised and maximised windows are left alone. A maximised
window already follows its monitor by itself. A minimised one has no
position worth keeping.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
